First, we expand the parenthesis and use the Pythagorean identity.

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})+\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘}))}^{2} & ={sin}^{2}⁡({105}^{∘})+2\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘})+{cos}^{2}⁡({105}^{∘}) \\  & =[{sin}^{2}⁡({105}^{∘})+{cos}^{2}⁡({105}^{∘})]+2\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘}) \\  & =1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={105}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {105}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({210}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({180}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain

$$
1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘})=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{(\operatorname{sin}⁡({105}^{∘})+\operatorname{cos}⁡({105}^{∘}))}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$
